name: Wolverine WVR-6R — silhouette study
notes: New independent WVR-6R silhouettes with left dorsal six-port rack and right forearm cannon. No inherited humanoid component generator. Shape review 2: remove inaccurate chest port mass, simplify shoulder launcher, keep forearm cannon smaller than whole chest. Reference iteration 3: independently traced ten-sided angular chest and forebody, sloped shoulder cowlings, tall rectangular six-port rack beside helmet, and narrow angular pilot helmet rather than bulbous cylinders. Reference iteration 4: broken-up wide shoulder shields, one clenched fist, distinctly separate cannon shroud in right arm, angular knee/thigh guards and narrower reverse-taper greaves. Fifth pass: separate armored hip section bridges chest and leg roots; individual six SRM bores remain on high asymmetric left launcher. Pass 6: individually framed six-port missile rack with physically carved 2x3 launch openings. Pass 7: hollow right-arm AC5 muzzle frame and hand with individually shaped knuckles and thumb, with no dangling fingers. Pass 8: replace rounded Wolverine torso masses with planar swept armor cowlings, bring shoulder pads closer to reference and reduce shared overlap along the shoulder seams. Shape pass 9: leaned chamfered pauldron armor, forward rectangular visor helmet and thin radio antennas, broad shouldered segmented chest. References WVR-6R FSW ink and multiple miniature viewpoints. Pass 10: replaced hollow-appearing pauldron caps with solid tapered shoulder-shell contours; split the single hexagonal chest into two swept structural breastplates. Pass 11: chamfered plate-sided WVR pauldrons with hard flat faces (not ovals) and defined projecting shin fairings at knee-to-ankle; checked against WVR-6R FSW drawing. Pass 12: replace egg-like shoulder cylinders with canted eight-sided armor shields of intentionally drawn front-facing x/y profiles, per WVR-6R FSW line art. Pass 13: vertically separate reference-accurate hip and upper torso: stretch the individually authored leg shapes to 34 grid units while translating the unmodified upper components 7 units, preventing stubby limb-to-torso appearance. Pass 14: compared WVR-6R FSW front illustration, SYZ dual pose, alternate CAD two perspectives. Shrink outer side torso blocks and cant the upper-arm plates so the torso is separated from shoulders by real geometry rather than enormous oval shoulder balls. Pass 15: WVR miniature comparison drove narrower hard-shoulder guards and shallow upper chest shields, replacing the large drooping pointed breastplates in Godot render. Pass 16: WVR-6R FSW front and posed resin show a flatter V-shaped breastplate and unmistakably long forearm cannon. Shallow angular torso plates plus forward-projecting AC5 cradle. Pass 17: WVR-6R leg plates redrawn as six-faced angular tapered thigh/shin solids matching the FSW front and dual-posed miniatures. Target is visibly different from Atlas rounded heavy leg armor, not more polygons or damage detail. Pass 18: WVR6R upright faceted pauldron shields now have rising pitched roofs and narrow lower anchors. AC/5 forearm shroud is angled forward rather than a drooping generic arm block. Pass 19: alternate WVR-6R pose motivated a sharply roofed swept plate rather than a pill. Angular shin fronts are now explicit separate armor geometry, not detail overlay. Pass 20: WVR-6R cannon stays on the forearm, with a long narrow box muzzle distinctly separated from its missile shoulder and chest armor; correct model-specific silhouette. Pass 22: matched WVR-6R three-quarter CGL/SYZ and AfterDark: shrink central shoulder root, lengthen flat canted upper-arm shield with 8-corner bevel, maintain real gap to ribcage, push separate rectangular pilot visor forward. Pass 23: six-vertex angular front shoulder shields replace ellipse-like WVR pauldrons; expose independent left/right mechanical knee joint under shortened upper-thigh armor, following the WVR-6R CGL plate/leg reference. Pass 24: rebuild WVR knee/shin as a canted forward knee wedge over a slimmer planar shin, in contrast to Atlas's straight armor slab. Source silhouettes based on AfterDark and SYZ two-view photos. Pass 25 CGL first: use actual plastic beginner box Wolverine and 2024 premium assembled three-quarter pose to bound shoulder breadth and preserve slim cannon-arm gap; not resin proxy exaggerated pauldrons. CGL pass 26: distinct compact Wolverine helmet with horizontal recessed visor and raised aft thruster hump. Avoid Atlas-style skull face; source is assembled CGL premium miniature. CGL pass27: 2019 and Premium Wolverine photos show a comparatively slim long AC5 forearm gun, not the earlier overly wide Atlas-like cannon bar; narrow muzzle and move inward, preserving independent RA part. CGL pass28: slimmer Wolverine wedge-toe feet and short kneecaps with exposed actuator yokes instead of Atlas assault weight rectangular double boot toe guards. CGL pass29: after pass28 actual render, reduce WVR upper armor plate height and width so shoulder no longer looks as large as Atlas's rounded assault bells; preserve upright shield and thinner exposed elbow. CGL plastic pass 32: Beginner Box WVR-6R and Catalyst premium Wolverine multi-angle photos prioritized. Narrowed inner pauldron edges and created visible articulated connection under the shield. Arms remain asymmetric; no cloned Atlas arm. CGL plastic pass 34: reduced Wolverine forearm bloat, added a real taper at elbow-to-fist and AC5 shroud, redrew thighs as narrow faceted sections instead of Atlas-like tree-trunks. Keep 55-ton gait clear from Atlas's heavy legs. CGL plastic pass 36: corrected bloated Wolverine AC/5 forearm housing, reducing 7-wide by 11-long tube to compact square 5-wide by 9-long housing with recessed rear throat, maintaining independent raised cannon arm. Pass 39 (CGL Wolverine Premium 2025 + 2019 AGoAC front and left 3/4): shorter faceted pauldrons, restored smaller joint cores. Relieved bloating and maintained cannon-arm asymmetry. Pass 41 (front/side silhouette overlap audit): small interior hip bearing cores bridge pelvis-to-thigh missing contacts without bulking outer armor; paired mirrored parts maintain pivot symmetry. CGL plastic pass39: AGOAC Wolverine front and side pauldron roofs narrower and more canted than previous large oval slabs, preserved independent shoulder joints with 2-3 grid overlap into upper arm; AC5 stays right arm. CGL pass42: Wolverine AGOAC front shows much narrower torso-root width than Atlas. Side torso shells now taper inward while launcher remains on left shoulder; maintain actual shoulder yoke and cannon root to prevent detached appearance. CGL plastic pass45: AGOAC Wolverine shoulder-mounted SRM6 flattened and lowered into the left collar instead of towering above its small cockpit. Retain six physically empty 2x3 forward mouths and chassis-specific asymmetric right arm cannon. CGL shape pass47 joint audit: placed a slim internal right elbow connection between asymmetrically cannon-equipped forearm and upper-arm armor, joining them through actual occupied cells while keeping outer negative space. Plastic-weighted pass49: AGOAC Wolverine and official premium front/3-4: trim both outer shoulder-shell and pauldron margins, flatten drooping breastplates and keep narrower CGL medium-torso proportions. Plastic-weighted pass52: AGOAC Wolverine has small angled outer shoulder caps with narrow elbow/forearm, not a second 100t Atlas. Reduced outer arm/shield overhang and tall corners, narrow cannon-side limb and left thigh with negative space retained. CGL plastic pass52: flatten inflated breast plates and add a recessed central chassis keel instead of generic twin blisters.
